words.trans: 控制自己的情绪、冷静下来、振作起来
examples: He had to get a grip on himself before going back in.

words.trans: adj. 裸露的、没有任何遮挡的；文中修饰 bulb（灯泡），指没有灯罩、光秃秃的灯泡
examples: A single bare bulb hung from the ceiling.

words.word: get down on one's hands and knees
words.trans: 四肢着地（双膝跪地、双手撑地）；文中指 Tom 为看清地缝而趴跪在地的特定姿势
words.key: get down on one's hands and knees
examples: Tom got down on his hands and knees to peer into the crack.

words.trans: v. 辨认出、想起（某人或某物的身份或来源）；couldn’t quite place 一时间想不起来、无法确切辨别，常用于对某种声音/味道/面孔熟悉却卡壳说不上来
examples: The voice was familiar, but he couldn't quite place it.

words.trans: v.（皮肤）刺痛、发麻，微微震颤，激动兴奋；n. 麻刺感、一阵酥麻
examples: His scalp tingled with fear.

words.trans: v. 摔倒、翻滚、滚落、暴跌、仓促行动；n. 跌倒、翻滚、一堆杂乱之物
examples: She tumbled down the steps and rolled over.

words.trans: adj. 滔滔不绝的、过分热情的、喷涌的；v.（gush 现在分词）喷涌、大肆抒发情感
examples: She gave a gushing account of the whole adventure.

words.trans: n. 楼梯井、楼梯间（整段楼梯所在的封闭空间）
examples: The shout echoed down the cold stairwell.

words.trans: 希望渺茫的尝试、孤注一掷、胜算很小（不等于完全没希望，只是几率低）；It’s a long shot but I’ll try. 机会渺茫，但我还是要试一试
examples: It's a long shot, but the key might still fit.

words.trans: n. 剪影、轮廓、黑色侧影；v. 使现出轮廓、使成剪影
examples: A figure stood in silhouette against the grey window.

words.trans: v. 猛拉、拽、用力扯；n. 猛拉、用力一拽；grabbed the key from the nail 从墙上那枚钉子上一把扯下钥匙
examples: He grabbed the key from the nail and gave it a sharp yank.

words.trans: n. 低沉微弱的嗡嗡声
examples: A low-level humming came from somewhere behind the wall.

words.trans: 只不过是、仅仅、几乎就是、充其量不过是，比 no more than 稍多一点。反向变体 little less than 几乎不亚于、差不多等于（It was little less than disaster. 这简直就是一场灾难）
examples: The room was little more than a concrete box.

words.trans: adj. 含硫的、硫酸的（英式 sulphuric，美式 sulfuric）；sulphuric acid 硫酸
examples: The water tasted faintly sulphuric, like rotten eggs.

words.trans: n.（香水、气味描写）调子、韵味、一丝气息，不是笔记、标记；background note 底层气息、隐隐的底色气味
examples: Under the disinfectant was a faint floral note.

words.trans: n. 地板清洁剂
examples: The whole place reeked of strong floor cleaner.

words.trans: adv. 一尘不染地、毫无污渍地
examples: The tiles were spotlessly, unnervingly clean.

words.trans: adv. 光秃秃地、刺眼地、毫无修饰地、鲜明地。①描写光线（本文用法）：灯光惨白、毫无装饰、刺眼生硬（The room was starkly lit by naked bulbs.）；②抽象语境：鲜明地、赤裸裸地（starkly different 截然不同）
examples: The room was starkly lit by naked bulbs.

words.trans: v.（clop 现在分词）（硬鞋底、马蹄）哒哒作响、踏得咯噔咯噔
examples: He heard boots clopping along the corridor.

words.trans: 固定表达，思绪、画面一股脑涌上心头
examples: A hundred questions crowded into his mind at once.

words.trans: n.（口语）疯子、变态恶棍
examples: Some psycho had smashed every window on the street.

words.trans: 用手顺着猫毛轻轻抚摸猫咪
examples: He stroked the cat slowly along its back as he talked.

words.trans: adv. 警惕地、小心翼翼地、戒备地
examples: The boy watched him warily, one hand on the door.

words.trans: adj. 上了清漆的、漆面光亮的（varnish 过去分词）
examples: The varnished wood gleamed in the harsh light.

words.trans: n. 镇纸
examples: A heavy glass paperweight held down the papers.

words.trans: 占据（面积、空间）；be taken up by sth（整片墙面空间）被某物占满
examples: A huge desk took up most of the floor.

words.trans: v. 忧思、郁郁沉思，闷闷地冥想
examples: He sat brooding in the corner for hours.

words.trans: adj. 雾气笼罩的、薄雾弥漫的
examples: Beyond the window lay a grey, misty morning.

words.trans: n.（复数 gullies）沟壑、溪谷，山体冲刷出的凹沟
examples: Rainwater had cut a deep gully across the slope.

words.trans: 侧重景象场面宏大、视觉冲击力强，不一定甜美，壮丽/苍凉也可（spectacular view / scenery）
examples: The view from the top was truly spectacular.

words.trans: adj.（描写说话）语速从容不迫、字字斟酌，每句都经过思量，语速偏慢审慎，有意识地控制措辞；used to being listened to 习惯于别人听自己讲话
examples: He spoke in a slow, deliberate voice, used to being listened to.

words.trans: 精神变态者（书面用词，小说正式词汇）
examples: The papers called the killer a cold-blooded psychopath.

words.trans: adj. 略带红色的、泛红的、淡红的。-ish 放在颜色后表示微微带点儿：reddish 泛红、yellowish 微黄、greyish 泛灰
examples: He had short, reddish hair and a pale complexion.

words.trans: 略微浮肿
examples: His eyes were slightly puffy, as if he hadn't slept.

words.trans: n. 面色、肤色（脸上皮肤）
examples: A blotchy red complexion coloured his face.

words.trans: v. 十指交扣、双手合拢握在一起；clasp one’s hands 双手互握（可攥紧也可松弛）
examples: He clasped his hands together on the desk.

words.trans: 学习吃力、学业陷入困境的学生、学困生
examples: The tutor stayed late to help a struggling student.

words.trans: n.（英国国教）教区牧师
examples: The vicar called round on Sunday mornings.

words.trans: n. 教区居民、教区信徒
examples: Every parishioner knew the old man's habits.

words.trans: n. 主谋、策划者、幕后首脑
examples: Police were still hunting the mastermind of the plot.

words.trans: adj.（声音）尖细单薄、细弱的嗓音（文学高频）
examples: He had a thin, reedy voice that was hard to take seriously.

words.trans: 伸手一把抓住并紧紧攥住不放，重点落到抓牢这个状态
examples: She grabbed hold of his arm to stop him going.

words.trans: 镇定下来、收拢心神、回过神
examples: She paused, gathering her wits before she spoke.

words.trans: v. ①发出隆隆轰鸣（雷声、肚子咕噜、车辆轰鸣）；②英式俚语（本句）看穿、识破、发觉秘密（We’ve been rumbled! 我们暴露了；He rumbled their plot. 他识破了他们的阴谋）
examples: 'They've been rumbled,' the sergeant muttered — their plan was found out.

words.trans: adj. 做好准备的；悬在上方蓄势待发。①物体悬于上方摆好即将行动的姿态；②描写人镇定自若、沉着（She was poised for action; a poised woman）；hold sth poised over 把某物举在……上方还没落下
examples: He held the pen poised over the paper, not writing.

words.trans: v. 来回摇摆、摇动；wag a finger at somebody 对着某人摆动一根手指（多为食指左右摇晃）
examples: The old man wagged a finger at the children.

words.trans: adv. 英勇地、壮举般地
examples: He pretended to work heroically through the whole night.

words.trans: adv. 无意地、不知情地、非故意地
examples: She had unwittingly led them straight to the hideout.

words.trans: adj. 避险的、闪避的；take evasive action 固定术语（航海/军事）采取避险闪避行动
examples: He took evasive action, steering sharply away.

words.trans: 英国刑事法庭里被告人站立的围栏位置、被告席
examples: The defendant stood silent in the dock.

words.trans: v. 讯问、盘问、审问
examples: The lawyer interrogated the witness without raising his voice.

words.trans: n.（英国）出庭大律师。英国律师分两类：barrister 出庭大律师，做辩护质询、可上高等法院；solicitor 事务律师，多做办公室工作、一般不上高等法庭
examples: A sharp young barrister handled the questioning.

words.trans: 英式俚语，不是瓶子，=guts/nerve/courage 胆量、勇气、硬气。have a bit of bottle 有几分胆量、敢硬撑；lose your bottle 怂了、泄气；bottle it 临阵退缩、打退堂鼓
examples: 'You've got more bottle than I gave you credit for,' the man said.

words.trans: 不等于“你很好/对你有好处”，而是算你有种！好样的！真有你的！表示赞许、认可对方所作所为
examples: 'You stood up to him? Good for you.'

words.trans: 飞快地随手翻阅、快速扫过，一般不逐字细读，手指快速一拨一页页过，侧重浏览翻查而非认真阅读
examples: He flicked through a file of old photographs.

words.trans: vi.（文学动词）猛地一惊、吓了一跳，身体不由自主地颤了一下，不是“开始”。老式书面义 start=give a sudden involuntary jump（受刺激身体猛然一抖、惊跳），不是大叫，是身体本能的一颤
examples: The quiet way he spoke made Tom start with fright.

words.trans: adv. 使人消除戒备地、化解敌意地
examples: 'Sit down,' he said disarmingly, gesturing to a chair.

words.trans: n.（口语）不满、牢骚、怨言；have no gripe against sb 对某人并无不满、没有什么私怨
examples: I've no gripe against you personally.

words.trans: adv. 满怀温情地、亲昵地
examples: 'My old friend,' she said affectionately.

words.trans: 副词，一度、曾经，适合描述身份、职业、角色，突出那是人生当中一段往事、现状已改变（文学、小说高频）
examples: He was once a well-known teacher around here.

words.trans: （通过拖延、搪塞、不摊牌的手段）给自己争取缓冲时间，不是买来钟表时间，是争取喘息机会
examples: The delay bought them precious time to think.

words.trans: 固定习语（正式书面、小说高频），任由你来支配、调遣、使用
examples: 'My time is at your disposal,' he said.

words.trans: 对……很感兴趣、爱好……
examples: He's very into vintage motorbikes.

words.trans: 习语，综合几条线索、碎片信息自己推导出真相，把几件事联系起来悟出原委
examples: She was slow to put two and two together.

words.trans: adj. 一时心血来潮的、临时起意的，事先没有计划
examples: It was a spur-of-the-moment decision, not a plan.

words.trans: 原本一时语塞、不知道该说什么，现在终于想好说辞、开口；找回自己的表达
examples: He stood frozen for a moment, then found his voice.

words.trans: 塔状手势/指尖塔。两手十指尖两两对碰、手掌分开留出空隙，形成像教堂尖塔一样的三角形空洞。寓意①自信、深思、权衡、分析思考（本场景审讯者 Rufus 听完说辞后摆出，冷静审视对方）；②也可表示优越感、胸有成竹
examples: He listened with his fingertips together in a steeple-gesture.

words.trans: 事情一步步展开、事态的真实经过
examples: He described how the events unfolded that night.

words.trans: 连词性习语，恰恰相反
examples: 'Not scared?' — 'On the contrary, I'm furious.'

words.trans: 行动带着强烈目的性、胸有成竹、有意为之，不是漫无目的、临时冲动
examples: Everything about him suggested a man acting with great purpose.

words.trans: 基于……、凭借……
examples: On the basis of what he'd heard, he had to act.

words.trans: 脸色凝固，面部肌肉绷紧，不再有任何柔和表情（like rock 如同岩石一般）；under the surface 表象之下（外表看不出来）
examples: His face was set like rock, betraying nothing.

words.trans: 不用着急、慢慢来；嘴上客套，并不是真的不紧迫
examples: 'No rush,' the man said, though his eyes were cold.
